observedSigns: Dark brown leaf spots with pale green edges
Yellowing and dying of leaves
Progression of symptoms starting from lower leaves moving upward
possibleCauses: Early Blight (Alternaria fungal infection), commonly triggered by warm, humid weather
Septoria leaf spot or other fungal leaf diseases
Bacterial leaf spot
Late Blight (if cool and very wet conditions persist)
followUpQuestions: Do the brown spots have visible concentric rings (resembling a target pattern) inside them?
Are you seeing any dark spots, lesions, or rot on the stems or fruits?
Is this issue affecting isolated plants or spreading across the entire field?
immediateActions: Carefully remove and destroy (burn or bury deep) the affected lower leaves to prevent fungal spores from spreading.
Avoid touching healthy plants immediately after handling diseased leaves, and sanitize your tools.
Water plants directly at the base rather than using overhead watering to keep foliage dry.
Stake plants and clear weeds to improve air circulation around the base of the crop.
assessment.whenToSeekHelp: Consult a local agricultural extension worker or farm adviser promptly if the leaf spotting spreads rapidly despite removing affected leaves, or if stems and fruits begin developing lesions.

uncertainty.reason: Diagnosis relies entirely on text description without photos to inspect spot patterns, stem condition, or fruit health.
